components.name: Button
components.summary: Starts an action, or goes to a destination as a link, alone, icon-only, confirmed in place, copying a value or connected in a group.
useWhen: Starting an action, such as saving or sending
A prominent destination, such as the next step of a flow
A familiar action as an icon alone, in a dense place (IconButton)
An action that takes effect at once and can't be undone (ConfirmButton)
Copying a value, such as a link or an ID (CopyButton)
Related actions that belong together (ButtonGroup)

avoidWhen.text: A destination inside running text.
Choosing one of a few views or filters that stays selected.
A setting that turns on or off.
A list of actions that would crowd a toolbar.
A consequence that needs a choice or typed confirmation before it happens.

examples.name: DismissTip
examples.title: Dismiss tip
examples.description: An IconButton with the Close cross closes, dismisses or removes what it sits in. Name it Close in the application's language, or say what it removes where several sit together.

examples.name: PendingAction
examples.title: Pending action
examples.description: While its work runs, a spinner replaces the content at the same size, and presses do nothing.

examples.name: ConfirmInPlace
examples.title: Confirm in place
examples.description: ConfirmButton arms on the first press and acts on the second. <kbd>Esc</kbd>, leaving it or 4 seconds disarm it. Its armed label is short and has no question mark: the verb, or the verb and object, "Remove Sam".

examples.name: CopyValue
examples.title: Copy value
examples.description: CopyButton copies a value and shows Copied, or Couldn’t copy, for about two seconds.

examples.name: QuietToolbar
examples.title: In a toolbar
examples.description: A button without a variant of its own takes its container's, such as ghost in a toolbar.

examples.name: ButtonLinks
examples.title: Links
examples.description: A button can go to a page instead of acting; Link says when a destination takes a button's shape.

examples.name: OnePrimaryAction
examples.title: Do: One primary button per group, at the end of its actions.

examples.name: SeveralPrimaryActions
examples.title: Don't: Several primary buttons: none of them stands out.

examples.name: ExplainWhatIsMissing
examples.title: Do: Let people press it, then show what is missing.

examples.name: DisabledUntilValid
examples.title: Don't: A disabled button that doesn’t say why.

examples.name: SayWhatWillHappen
examples.title: Labels
examples.description: Start with a verb and say what will happen, and when the outcome is known, put it in the label.

components.name: Toolbar
components.summary: A bar of icon buttons for one subject, such as an editor's formatting, in a row or a column.
useWhen: Controls for one subject, such as an editor's formatting
Many icon-only actions that would each take a tab stop
A palette whose chosen tool stays chosen, such as drawing tools

avoidWhen.text: A form's or a dialog's actions, which keep a tab stop each.
Buttons joined into one connected control, such as a main action and its menu.
A choice of one view or filter, shown as a selected segment.
An application's menus of commands, such as File and Edit.
A page's search, filters and primary action, where fields keep their arrow keys.

examples.name: DrawingTools

examples.name: ViewControls

examples.name: PageToolbar

examples.name: CenteredContent
examples.title: Alignment
examples.description: Each child is as wide as the column by default, or keeps its own width at the start, the middle or the end. Buttons, chips and badges keep their own width in any case.

examples.name: NestedSpacing
examples.title: Do: A larger gap between sections and a smaller one inside them.

examples.name: OneGapForAll
examples.title: Don't: One gap for everything: the sections run together.

components.name: Grid
components.summary: Grid lays out content in columns, a set number, a template or as many as fit, with even gaps.
useWhen: Items of one kind in as many columns as fit, such as cards or stats
A main column beside a narrower one, such as a summary and its details
Content lined up in a set number of equal columns

avoidWhen.text: Content top to bottom, one item per line.
A few items side by side at their own widths, such as actions.
Rows of data that people sort, select or compare.
Two panes people resize, or a list beside its detail.
One block with an inset or a size container, and no columns.
A layout that changes by the window class rather than by what fits.

examples.name: FittingColumns
examples.title: Do: A minimum width, so the grid fits the columns to its own width.

examples.name: FixedColumns
examples.title: Don't: Three columns in a narrow pane: each card is squeezed.

guides.name: setup
guides.title: Install the private package
guides.summary: Registry access, styles, themes and public entry points.

guides.name: migration
guides.title: Migrate an interface to envUI
guides.summary: Replace existing UI while preserving application behavior.

guides.name: customizing
guides.title: Customize and extend
guides.summary: Give one element colors of its own or recolor an area, compose components into the application's own, and style their parts.

guides.name: agent-tooling
guides.title: For agents
guides.summary: The AGENTS.md index, the MCP server, the manifest, llms.txt and the skills that coding agents use.

guides.name: writing
guides.title: Writing
guides.summary: The words of an interface built with envUI: voice, capitalisation, action words, numbers and dates, and wording ready for translation.

guides.name: dev-mode
guides.title: Dev mode
guides.summary: Check a page's layout while developing: the readout and its problems for agents, at any width, and a 3D view with an inspector for people.

foundations.name: colors
foundations.title: Colors & themes
foundations.summary: Colors named by their role, so every screen works in light, dark and high contrast.

foundations.name: typography
foundations.title: Typography
foundations.summary: A few text styles, each with one job, from a page's hero line to small notes.

foundations.name: spacing
foundations.title: Spacing & density
foundations.summary: How space groups things, controls line up, the compact scale and tighter rows, and what corners say.

foundations.name: responsive
foundations.title: Adapting to width
foundations.summary: Components follow the space they sit in, and four window classes name where a layout changes.

foundations.name: icons
foundations.title: Icons
foundations.summary: Thousands of Material Symbols that follow their text, outlined or filled.

foundations.name: accessibility
foundations.title: Accessibility
foundations.summary: What every component does for keyboard, screen readers, contrast, motion and touch, and what an app still supplies.

patterns.name: forms
patterns.title: Form layout and validation
patterns.summary: Ask for information in a form, check it, and help people fix what's wrong.
useWhen: Several answers, given and submitted together
Finding and fixing what a form refused

avoidWhen.text: A single setting that takes effect at once.
Deleting or removing something, with undo or a confirmation.
Narrowing a list or a table as people choose, without submitting.

examples.name: CreateProject
examples.title: Create project
examples.description: The aim is a form people get right on the first submit.

examples.name: ValidationTiming
examples.title: Validation timing
examples.description: On submit first: show each field's error, and move focus to the error summary, or straight to the field when there is only one. Then as people leave a field they have typed in. Never while they type, though an error goes as soon as the value is right.

examples.name: ServerError
examples.title: Server error
examples.description: While the form is sent, its submit button shows that it is working: it keeps its size and ignores presses. When the server refuses or can't be reached, keep everything people entered, and move focus to an Alert at the top that says what to do.

examples.name: ErrorSummary
examples.title: Error summary
examples.description: After a refused submit, a danger Alert titled "There is a problem" lists each error as a Link that moves focus to its field. It is read once, as it takes focus, with no announcement of its own.

examples.name: GroupedChoices
examples.title: Grouped choices
examples.description: Several checkboxes go in a group whose name says what they are for, as the choices of a RadioGroup do.

examples.name: LongFormInSteps
examples.title: A long form in steps
examples.description: A long form splits into a few short steps, each a page of its own with its fields. Progress, split into steps, says where people are; Continue checks the step's fields before moving on, Back keeps every answer, and the last step shows the answers before the form's own action.

examples.name: OneColumn
examples.title: Do: One column, read top to bottom, with the action after the last field.
examples.description: A date, a time or a month each have a picker of their own, which people can also type into. | Control | Use for | | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | Date picker | A day, such as a due date or a start date. | | Time picker | A time of day, such as when a meeting starts. | | Month picker | A month, such as a report's period or a card's expiry date. |

examples.name: SideBySide
examples.title: Don't: Fields side by side: people miss the one beside their path.

patterns.name: settings
patterns.title: Settings
patterns.summary: Let people change how the application works for them, and see each change apply.
useWhen: A preference that applies at once, such as a notification or the theme
A few related values saved together, such as a profile

avoidWhen.text: Several answers given once and submitted together, such as creating something.
A choice that filters or changes the view of the page people are on.
Deleting an account or a workspace.

examples.name: ImmediateToggles
examples.title: Immediate toggles
examples.description: Each setting either applies the moment it changes, or waits with the settings it depends on for a Save button, and the two never share a section.

examples.name: SaveSection
examples.title: Save a section
examples.description: Settings that only make sense together wait for a Save button. A Badge marks the section while it holds unsaved changes, and Cancel puts back what was saved.

examples.name: AppearanceChoice
examples.title: Appearance
examples.description: The theme applies at once. The scale, comfortable or compact, is one for the whole application: it never changes for one page or one section.

examples.name: DangerZone
examples.title: Danger zone
examples.description: The last section, apart from the rest, holds what deletes or ends the account or the workspace, confirmed as destructive actions are.

examples.name: SwitchesApplyAtOnce
examples.title: Do: Switches that apply the moment they change, with no Save button.

examples.name: SwitchesWithSave
examples.title: Don't: Switches that wait for Save: people can't tell which changes are kept.

patterns.name: destructive-actions
patterns.title: Destructive actions
patterns.summary: Let people delete, remove or archive with as little friction as is safe, and undo or confirm by what is at stake.
useWhen: Deleting, removing, archiving or ending something
An action that affects others or can't be undone

avoidWhen.text: A decision that needs fields or several choices, beyond a confirmation.
Reporting the outcome of an action that people can't change.

examples.name: UndoInstead
examples.title: Undo instead
examples.description: Asking "Are you sure?" before everything trains people to confirm without reading. Archiving here happens at once, and a toast offers Undo, which puts the item back where it was.

examples.name: TypeToConfirm
examples.title: Type to confirm
examples.description: Where an action can't be undone and reaches many people or much work, the dialog asks for the name. Its confirm button stays enabled: a wrong name keeps the dialog open and says what to type.

examples.name: BulkDelete
examples.title: Bulk delete
examples.description: The count is in the button, the question and the confirm button: "Delete 2 documents…".

examples.name: DangerKeptForDelete
examples.title: Do: The danger tone only on what deletes or ends something.
examples.description: Match the friction to what is at stake. | Friction | Use for | | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Undo in a toast | An action that can be undone, and that people take often. | | Confirm in place | An action that can't be undone, with little at stake, through a ConfirmButton. | | Confirm in a dialog | Deleting something people made, or something that affects others, through a danger ConfirmDialog. | | Type the name | An action that can't be undone and reaches many people or much work. |

examples.name: DangerEverywhere
examples.title: Don't: Every action in the danger tone: none of them stands out.

patterns.name: file-upload
patterns.title: File upload
patterns.summary: Let people add files, follow each upload, and put right the ones that fail.
useWhen: Several files that upload as soon as they are added
Attachments to a form, sent once they are up

avoidWhen.text: One file, such as a logo, sent with its form.
One task over many files that succeeds or fails as a whole, such as an import.
Deleting files that can't come back, with a confirmation.

examples.name: UploadFiles
examples.title: Upload files
examples.description: Each file uploads as soon as it is added, in its own row of a list under the drop zone: a bar while it goes up, its size once it is there, or what went wrong with Try again.

examples.name: TurnedAway
examples.title: Turned away
examples.description: A file of the wrong kind or too large never joins the list. The zone says which file and why, and takes the others.

examples.name: FailedUpload
examples.title: Failed upload
examples.description: The file keeps its row, with what went wrong and Try again, which starts it over. The other files go on uploading.

examples.name: RemoveWithUndo
examples.title: Remove with undo
examples.description: Remove takes the file out of the list at once and stops its upload, and a toast offers Undo, as destructive actions describe.

examples.name: AttachInForm
examples.title: In a form
examples.description: The files upload while people fill in the rest. A send waits for any still going up, then goes with them.

examples.name: ZoneStaysReady
examples.title: Do: The zone stays ready for more while each file's row shows its upload.

examples.name: ZoneBusyWhileUploading
examples.title: Don't: The whole zone busy until every file is up: people wait to add the next.

patterns.name: feedback
patterns.title: Notifications and feedback
patterns.summary: Tell people what happened, what state things are in and what needs them, in the place and at the volume each message deserves.
useWhen: The outcome of an action, or of work in the background
A state people should notice, on a page, a row or a destination

avoidWhen.text: A value that is wrong in a form.
Content that is loading.
A region with nothing to show.
Undo after a delete, or a confirmation before one.

examples.name: SaveConfirmation
examples.title: Save confirmation
examples.description: Each message is announced at most once, and only what calls for action interrupts. The outcome of an action people started is a toast.

examples.name: SectionAlert
examples.title: A condition of the page
examples.description: An Alert that is there when the page loads describes it and offers the one thing people can do.

examples.name: BackgroundTask
examples.title: Background work
examples.description: When the export ends, a toast with Download reaches people wherever they are, and the page keeps a link to the file too.

examples.name: StatusInRows
examples.title: Status in rows
examples.description: One tone per status, everywhere.

examples.name: StatusInWords
examples.title: Do: Each status in its own words, with the tone adding to them.
examples.description: Put each message where it belongs, at the volume it deserves. | Message | Use for | | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | A field's error | A value in a field that is wrong, as forms show it. | | An Alert on the page | A condition of the page, read with the page. | | An announced Alert | Something that just happened and must interrupt. | | A toast | The outcome of an action people started, announced politely. | | A danger toast | An action that failed where the page can't show it, with Try again. | | A confirmation | A decision people must make, in a ConfirmDialog. | | A badge | The state of a row, read with the row, in a Badge. |

examples.name: StatusInColor
examples.title: Don't: The same word in every tone: only the color tells them apart.

patterns.name: loading
patterns.title: Loading
patterns.summary: Show that something is loading, in the place and shape of what is coming, without implying how long it takes.
useWhen: A page, a region or a result that takes a noticeable while
Work with a measurable end, such as an upload

avoidWhen.text: Files uploading, each with its own progress.
Content that turned out empty, or that failed to load.

examples.name: CardsLoading
examples.title: Cards loading
examples.description: Where the shape is known, the page renders its own components as skeletons over placeholder items, so its code is the same loading and loaded.

examples.name: SkeletonList
examples.title: Skeleton list
examples.description: Placeholder items give the components stand-ins to render, and text that hasn't arrived shows as a bar the length of its text style. Show the skeleton only once a load takes a noticeable moment, so quick loads never flash it.

examples.name: SearchResultsLoading
examples.title: No known shape
examples.description: A Spinner says what is loading beside it.

examples.name: PendingButton
examples.title: An action
examples.description: The button that saves shows the work in progress.

examples.name: UploadProgress
examples.title: Measurable work
examples.description: Progress measures each file.

examples.name: PageProgress
examples.title: A whole page
examples.description: The top bar's progress bar shows the next page is on its way.

examples.name: SkeletonInPlace
examples.title: Do: The content's own components as a skeleton, where it will appear.
examples.description: Show what is coming in its place and shape where you can, and say only that something is on its way where you can't. | Indicator | Use for | | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- | | A skeleton | Content of a known shape, in its own components. | | A spinner with its label | Content of no known shape, such as search results. | | A spinner beside it | An update to what is already shown. | | A pending button | The result of an action, on the button that started it. | | A progress bar | Work whose end can be measured, such as an upload. | | The top bar's progress | A whole page on its way. |

examples.name: SpinnerInPlace
examples.title: Don't: A spinner for content of a known shape: the page jumps when it lands.

examples.name: RefreshInPlace
examples.title: Do: Content that refreshes stays, with a Spinner beside it.

examples.name: SkeletonOnRefresh
examples.title: Don't: Content turned back into a skeleton to refresh: people lose their place.

patterns.name: empty-states
patterns.title: Empty states
patterns.summary: Show what a region holds when it has nothing to show, tell first use from no results, done and failed, and offer the one way on.
useWhen: A list, a table or a page with nothing to show
A search or filters that match nothing
Content that failed to load, or that people may not see
A whole page that can't show, such as one not found

avoidWhen.text: Content that is still loading.
Reporting that an action, such as a save, failed.

examples.name: FirstUse
examples.title: First use
examples.description: The state takes the place of the list or the table, under the heading and toolbar that stay: an icon, a heading, a sentence and the one action. Until something exists, it holds the create action; then the page's own action takes over.

examples.name: NoResults
examples.title: No results
examples.description: The search and the filters stay, and Clear filters resets them, as in filtering.

examples.name: LoadFailed
examples.title: Load failed
examples.description: A failure is a danger Alert, announced as it appears, in the room the table takes; it says the documents are safe.

examples.name: NoAccess
examples.title: No access
examples.description: The state says who to ask, and Request access sends the request.

examples.name: AllDone
examples.title: All done
examples.description: When the last review is approved, the queue says so, and what comes next.

examples.name: WholePage
examples.title: A whole page
examples.description: When the whole page can't show, because its address leads nowhere, the person may not see it or the device is offline, the frame stays and the page says so, with the way on: Go to Home, Request access or Try again.

examples.name: OneAction
examples.title: Do: One action, the one that ends the state.
examples.description: Each kind says something different, and offers a different way on. | Kind | Use for | | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | First use | Nothing has been made yet. | | No results | A search or a filter matches nothing. | | All done | People cleared a queue, such as their reviews. | | Load failed | The content couldn't load, as a danger Alert. | | No access | The content exists, but not for this person. | | A whole page | The page can't show at all: not found, no access or offline. |

examples.name: CompetingActions
examples.title: Don't: Several actions compete, and none says what ends the state.

patterns.name: key-figures
patterns.title: Key figures
patterns.summary: Show the few labelled figures that sum up a view, such as a dashboard's, with how each changed and over what period.
useWhen: The few figures that sum up a view, such as a dashboard's
A figure and how it changed, such as 12 percent up on last month

avoidWhen.text: Many values to compare or sort, such as figures for each project.
A quantity within a known range, such as the seats assigned of a plan's five.
A count on a control, such as unread messages on a tab.
A figure that changes while people look at it.

examples.name: ProjectHealth
examples.title: Project health
examples.description: A key figure is a muted label, a large figure and a Badge that says how it changed, with the period beside it. A Surface holds a few of them in a Grid.

examples.name: OnAPane
examples.title: On a pane
examples.description: A group on a pane takes the muted fill, so its figures stand apart; the pane's heading names it.

examples.name: InACard
examples.title: One figure
examples.description: A Card frames a single figure.

patterns.name: conversation
patterns.title: Conversation
patterns.summary: Talk with an assistant or with other people, and follow each reply as it arrives.
useWhen: A chat with an assistant whose replies stream in
Messages between people, such as a support chat or a team thread

avoidWhen.text: Comments on one item, read more often than written.
A short notice that comes and goes, such as Message sent.
Several answers given together and submitted once.

examples.name: AssistantChat
examples.title: Assistant chat
examples.description: The log of messages takes the space and scrolls, and the composer stays at its foot, so the draft is always in reach. An assistant's answers are formatted text, with Copy once they are complete.

examples.name: FirstMessage
examples.title: First message
examples.description: Before anything is said, the log's place holds a short question and a few suggestions. Pressing one sends it as the first message; the composer is there from the start.

examples.name: StoppedReply
examples.title: Stopped reply
examples.description: Stop keeps what has arrived, marked as stopped, with Try again beside it. People can also simply write their next message.

examples.name: FailedSend
examples.title: Failed send
examples.description: The message stays in the log where it was written, marked as not sent, with Try again beside it. Nothing people wrote is lost, and the composer is free for the next message.

examples.name: BetweenPeople
examples.title: Between people
examples.description: Each message from someone else names its author and time. Replies arrive whole, so there is nothing to stop, and a message on its way says so until the server takes it.

examples.name: ReplyAsItArrives
examples.title: Do: The reply in the log as it arrives, so people read while it is written.

examples.name: WholeReplyAtOnce
examples.title: Don't: A spinner until the whole reply is ready: people wait with nothing to read.

patterns.name: filtering
patterns.title: Filtering and search
patterns.summary: Let people narrow a list or a table to what they want, see how many items match, and undo it in one step.
useWhen: A list or a table long enough to look for items in
Narrowing items by what they are, such as status, owner or type

avoidWhen.text: Opening a page, a project or a document by name from anywhere in the application.
Choosing values for a form people submit.
Putting a table's rows in order.
No results that match, and a way to widen the search.

examples.name: SearchAndFilters
examples.title: Search and filters
examples.description: A search and a few filters sit in the PageHeader's toolbar, above the results.

examples.name: FilterPanel
examples.title: Filters in a popover
examples.description: A Filters button, with a count of the filters in use, opens a Popover of checkboxes in groups that apply as they change.

examples.name: ActiveFilters
examples.title: Filters in use
examples.description: Each filter in use is a token named after it, "Status: Open", a small button with a close cross that removes it, beside Add filter and Clear filters.

examples.name: AppliedAtOnce
examples.title: Do: Each choice filters at once, and a count says how many match.

examples.name: WaitsForApply
examples.title: Don't: An Apply button for quick filters: nothing says what will match.

patterns.name: data-tables
patterns.title: Data tables
patterns.summary: Show many records in rows and columns that people can sort, page through, select and act on, also on narrow screens.
useWhen: Records compared by several values, such as owner, status and date
Sorting records, paging through them or acting on several at once

avoidWhen.text: Items with one or two values each, such as a list of documents and their editors.
Narrowing the rows to the ones people want.
Hierarchical items that open and close, such as folders.
A table with no rows yet, or none that match.
Deleting rows, with undo or a confirmation.

examples.name: SortAndPaginate
examples.title: Sort and paginate
examples.description: A Table holds the data, with its own sorting, selection and stacking, and Pagination below it gives the range, "1–4 of 6", working while the next set loads.

examples.name: SelectAndBulkActions
examples.title: Select and act on several rows
examples.description: While rows are selected, a bulk bar shows the count and its actions. Archive acts at once with Undo; Delete asks first.

examples.name: RowActions
examples.title: Row actions
examples.description: The name links to the record; the other actions wait in a Menu named for the row, "More actions for Website refresh".

patterns.name: progressive-disclosure
patterns.title: Progressive disclosure
patterns.summary: Show what most people need first, and keep the rest one step away, in the place and at the depth that fits it.
useWhen: Options, details or actions most people rarely need
An explanation of a term that would clutter the page

avoidWhen.text: Switching between views of the same content.
Moving between the places of the application.
Information people need to complete a task, such as a required field or an error.

examples.name: AdvancedOptions
examples.title: Advanced options
examples.description: Advanced options wait behind a Disclosure.

examples.name: ShowMore
examples.title: Show all
examples.description: The button stays after the list and says what a press does, "Show all 12", then "Show fewer", and tells assistive technology whether the whole list shows.

examples.name: DetailsInSheet
examples.title: Details in a sheet
examples.description: The list stays in place under the Sheet, so people continue from the row they opened.

examples.name: OverflowActions
examples.title: Overflow actions
examples.description: Share and Edit stay visible; the rest wait in a Menu named More actions.

examples.name: ExplainATerm
examples.title: Explain a term
examples.description: A help button opens a Popover with a short definition and a link.

patterns.name: app-frame
patterns.title: App frame
patterns.summary: Frame an application's screens with a Scaffold, a TopBar and the same destinations as a Bar, a Rail or a Drawer, by the width of the window.
useWhen: A handful of destinations, each with a page
An installed app that draws its own title bar

avoidWhen.text: Moving between views of one object, such as its overview and its activity.
Choosing between a bar, a rail and a drawer by the window's width.
A page's own title and actions.

examples.name: AppFrame
examples.title: App frame
examples.description: The app frame is one Scaffold at the application's root, around the router's outlet: a TopBar with the name, search and the account menu, the navigation, and the page in the body.

examples.name: MenuOnPhones
examples.title: A menu on phones
examples.description: With many destinations, or none with icons, a phone shows no bar: a menu button in the top bar opens the same Drawer in a Sheet.

examples.name: WithDetails
examples.title: Details beside the page
examples.description: Side content that is not navigation goes in a supporting pane of Panes, in the body.

examples.name: InstalledWindow
examples.title: An installed app's window
examples.description: An installed app that draws its own title bar runs it across the whole window, above the navigation, with a Menubar at its start where the app has one. Only the body scrolls below it, so the window's controls never cover a scrollbar.

examples.name: DestinationsInNavigation
examples.title: Do: Every destination in the navigation, and the page's own action in its header.

examples.name: DestinationsInTopBar
examples.title: Don't: More destinations in the top bar: people look for them in two places.

patterns.name: navigation
patterns.title: Navigation
patterns.summary: Let people move between the places of an application, see where they are, and find their way back.
useWhen: Several places people move between
Showing where people are and the way back up

avoidWhen.text: Showing more of the page's content without leaving the page.
Moving between pages of one long list.
A list beside the detail of its selected item.
A whole frame to copy, with the navigation and a top bar.

examples.name: PrimaryNavigation
examples.title: Primary navigation
examples.description: The primary navigation marks the current page, a trail leads back up from deep pages, and a search opens anything by name.

examples.name: Hierarchy
examples.title: Hierarchy
examples.description: The trail shows the levels above the page, each a link; the page itself is the last level and no link.

examples.name: ViewsOfOneThing
examples.title: Views of one thing
examples.description: Tabs switch the views of one project in place. Its settings are another page, so they are a link in the header's actions.

examples.name: ListAndDetail
examples.title: List and detail
examples.description: As narrow as a phone, the detail shows in place of the list, with a back button that names where it goes.

examples.name: TabsForViews
examples.title: Do: Tabs for the views of the one thing the page is about.
examples.description: Each kind of navigation answers its own need, and a page can use several. | Navigation | Use for | | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Destinations | The places of the application: one list, which the Scaffold shows as a bar, a rail or a drawer. | | Breadcrumbs | A page two or more levels down, on one line in its PageHeader. | | Tabs | Views of the object a page is about, under its header. | | Pager | Pages read in order, at the end of the content. | | Command palette | Opening anything by name, as CommandPalette shows. | | List and detail | A list whose items open beside it, in Panes. |

examples.name: TabsForPlaces
examples.title: Don't: Tabs for places of the application: they have no address of their own.

patterns.name: account-and-organizations
patterns.title: Account and organizations
patterns.summary: Show who is signed in and where, and give people their own things and their organizations from a menu in the frame.
useWhen: Account settings, the theme and Sign out on every page
People who belong to several organizations

avoidWhen.text: The application's places, such as Projects and Settings.
The frame the menus sit in, with its top bar and navigation.

examples.name: AvatarMenu
examples.title: Avatar menu
examples.description: Both are a Menu behind a trigger in the frame. The account menu opens from the person's AvatarButton at the end of the TopBar: their avatar, name and email first, then their own things, with Sign out last.

examples.name: WithOrganizations
examples.title: Organizations in the account menu
examples.description: A submenu switches between the person's organizations, and names the current one.

examples.name: SwitchOrganization
examples.title: A switcher of its own
examples.description: Where people switch often, a button at the top of the navigation Drawer, or at the start of the top bar, names the active organization and opens them all, with the person's role under each and an action that creates one. Before the first organization, that action is a button of its own.

examples.name: RowTrigger
examples.title: A row at the foot of the navigation
examples.description: The account menu's trigger can be a row with the avatar and the name, as wide as the drawer; the menu opens above it.

examples.name: AvatarTrigger
examples.title: Do: The person's own avatar, named by their name, at the end of the top bar.

examples.name: GenericTrigger
examples.title: Don't: The same icon for everyone: nothing says who is signed in.

examples.name: CurrentName
examples.title: Do: The switcher names the active organization.

examples.name: GenericLabel
examples.title: Don't: A generic label: nothing says where people are.

Accordion.Item.description: One section of an accordion: its heading, a button with a plus or minus at its start, and the panel below it.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading that opens and closes the section, in medium weight: say what the panel holds, such as a question it answers. Given as undefined, such as over a placeholder item, a skeleton shows a bar in its place.

props.name: children
props.description: The panel, in muted text lined up with the title, shown while the item is open.

props.name: value
props.description: Names the item in the accordion's value, for an accordion that is controlled or opens items at first. Without it, the item takes a generated one.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The item ignores presses and can't be focused; it stays dimmed.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Receives whether this item is open, each time it opens or closes.

Accordion.Root.description: A list of sections, each a heading that shows and hides its panel, separated by full-width hairlines. A plus at the start of a heading becomes a minus while its section is open. One item is open at a time unless `multiple` is set. Built on Base UI's Accordion.

props.name: children
props.description: The items: Accordion.Item, one for each section.

props.name: value
props.description: The values of the open items, for a controlled accordion: update it from onValueChange. Use defaultValue instead to leave it to the accordion.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The values of the items open at first, for an accordion that keeps its own state.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the values of the open items, each time an item opens or closes.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Lets several items be open at once; otherwise opening one closes the one that was open.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The level of each item's heading, for the page's outline; they look the same at every level.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Every item ignores presses and can't be focused.

props.name: hiddenUntilFound
props.description: Keeps closed panels in the page, hidden until found, so the browser's find in page reaches their text and opens the item that holds it, where the browser supports it.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows the component, and everything inside it, as a skeleton while its content loads: text becomes bars, icons, avatars, media and controls filled shapes of their size, and borders and corners stay. It is a busy region, and its content can't be focused or read until it loads. Turning it on or off renders its content anew, so state inside it starts over.

Alert.description: An inline banner for a page- or section-level message, in its tone. It stays a server component: its dismiss button is an IconButton with a cross, a client leaf named in the provider's language.

props.name: tone
props.description: What the message means: info, success, warning or danger, for an error or a failure. Sets the tint, the border and the icon; info and success alerts are also status messages.

props.name: title
props.description: A short heading for the message, such as "Sync paused", above the message.

props.name: children
props.description: The message: what it means and what people can do.

props.name: icon
props.description: Replaces the tone's icon; false shows none.

props.name: action
props.description: An action below the message, such as a Button or Link.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Shows a dismiss button that calls it; the application removes the alert.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the dismiss button, also shown as its tooltip.

props.name: announce
props.description: The alert appeared because of something that just happened and should interrupt: warning and danger alerts take the alert role. Info and success alerts are always polite status messages.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows the component, and everything inside it, as a skeleton while its content loads: text becomes bars, icons, avatars, media and controls filled shapes of their size, and borders and corners stay. It is a busy region, and its content can't be focused or read until it loads. Turning it on or off renders its content anew, so state inside it starts over.

AnimatedNumber.description: A number within text that rolls to its new value when it changes: up when it grows and down when it shrinks, so a count updated by other controls is noticed. The text is always the current value.

props.name: value
props.description: The number to show; when it changes, the new value rolls in, up as it grows, down as it shrinks.

props.name: formatValue
props.default: the number format of EnvUIProvider's locale, or else the browser's
props.description: Writes the value as text, such as a currency.

Avatar.description: A round picture of a person or organization, with the default person picture or initials as fallback.

props.name: name
props.description: Person or organization name: the accessible name of a named avatar, and the initials fallback.

props.name: src
props.description: Picture URL. The fallback shows while it loads and when it is missing or fails.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Shown without a picture: the default person picture, or initials (for example, for an organization).

props.name: hue
props.description: The fill behind the initials or the person picture. Without it, the name chooses one, the same for the same name everywhere; set it for an organization with a color of its own.

props.name: size
props.description: sm 1.5 rem, md 2 rem, lg 3 rem or xl 5.5 rem, such as for a profile page.

props.name: named
props.description: Names the avatar as an image by `name`. Without it, the avatar is hidden from assistive technology, for when text beside it already names the person.

props.name: selected
props.description: Shows the avatar as chosen, such as in a list of people to pick from: a ring around it and a small check at its bottom end, so the choice never rests on color alone. It is a look only: the control around the avatar, such as a checkbox or an option, says it is chosen.

AvatarButton.description: A person's avatar as a button, typically the account menu trigger in a topbar. A halo shows hover, press and an open menu, and the tooltip names the account.

props.name: name
props.description: The person's name: shown in the tooltip, and the accessible name unless aria-label is set.

props.name: description
props.description: A second tooltip line, such as the e-mail address of the signed-in account.

props.name: src
props.description: Picture URL; the default person picture shows without one.

props.name: fallback
props.description: Shown without a picture: the default person picture (default), or the initials of `name`.

props.name: size
props.description: The picture: sm 1.5 rem, md 2 rem or lg 3 rem, inside a slightly larger hit area, which grows to the touch height under a coarse pointer.

AvatarGroup.description: A pile of avatars for a set of people, such as the members of a project, with a chip that counts the rest and lists them in its tooltip. Hover, a tap or keyboard focus spreads it.

props.name: people
props.description: The people, in order. Pass a preview with total when there are many more.

props.name: max
props.description: The most avatars to show; the overflow chip after them counts the rest. All by default.

props.name: size
props.description: As Avatar: sm 1.5 rem, md 2 rem, lg 3 rem or xl 5.5 rem.

props.name: gather
props.description: The group keeps the room its spread takes, so spreading never moves what is around it, and the pile gathers at rest toward one end of that room: start, or end for a group at the end of a row, such as a list row's action.

props.name: total
props.description: How many people there are in all, when people is only a preview of them.

props.name: onPersonClick
props.description: Makes every avatar a button with a name tooltip; receives the person pressed. The avatars are targets only while the group is spread: at rest the pile is one target, which hover, a tap or keyboard focus spreads.

props.name: formatMore
props.description: Text for people beyond the list, in the overflow tooltip and the group's name. It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.avatarGroup.more` for this group.

props.name: formatLabel
props.description: The group's name from the number of people and their names, which end with formatMore's text for people counted in total but not listed, such as "3 people: Alex Morgan, Sam Lee, 1 more". It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.avatarGroup.label` for this group; aria-label replaces it.

Badge.description: A small pill label for a state, such as In progress, Blocked or Archived, or for neutral metadata, such as a plan or a count of seats; with count, a compact count, such as 12 unread.

props.name: icon
props.description: A decorative icon before the label, such as a check mark; hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: children
props.description: The label: a state, a name or a category in a word or two. It stays on one line and ends with an ellipsis where the badge is wider than its container.

props.name: count
props.description: A count, such as 12, or short text such as 99+, in place of a label: a compact round pill, in tabular figures, as beside a navigation label, in a tab or on a button.

props.name: tone
props.description: Meaning of the state; done is the purple of completed work. Neutral by default. A count in the accent tone, solid, draws attention, such as unread messages that need an answer.

props.name: variant
props.description: soft tints the background, solid fills it with the tone, outline draws a border.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: What the count means, such as 12 unread, which assistive technology reads in place of the number; the number alone otherwise.

Bar.description: The navigation bar for compact windows, such as phones: up to five destinations side by side, each an icon above its label, at the bottom of the window. A `nav` landmark; the current destination reports aria-current="page", and every destination is a tab stop.

props.name: destinations
props.description: The application's destinations, the same array Rail and Drawer take. Give the bar 3 to 5: past 5 it shows the first 4 and a More item that opens the rest in a menu. Groups don't show.

props.name: background
props.description: The bar's background, named as Surface's and Card's: default, the navigation's background, the default surface color, as a plain rectangle; page, the page's background, so it sits on the page. On a surface, such as a Sheet, both take the surface's color. Set it on its own, such as a Bar with page under a TopBar with its background.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the navigation landmark, such as Main or Project; give each landmark of a page its own.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows the component, and everything inside it, as a skeleton while its content loads: text becomes bars, icons, avatars, media and controls filled shapes of their size, and borders and corners stay. It is a busy region, and its content can't be focused or read until it loads. Turning it on or off renders its content anew, so state inside it starts over.

Box.description: A plain block for what needs no row or column of its own: an inset (`padding`), a size container (`container`) or a named node. It sizes to its content and never paints.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, for its meaning, such as render={<section />} or render={<ul />}, or another component to lay out without a wrapper, such as a Surface: the primitive's attributes merge into its props. It must forward native props and refs. A div by default.

props.name: ref
props.description: The rendered element, a div by default. Its type is the element type parameter, which a ref passed in sets: a ref to the element that render makes, such as useRef<HTMLElement>(null) with render={<section />}, type-checks.

props.name: name
props.description: A name for this node, such as "filters" or "summary", which dev mode and the docs show; it renders as `data-env-name`. A component's part class names its node instead.

props.name: container
props.description: Makes the element a size container of this name, for container queries on its inline size, such as container="filters" for `@container filters (width >= 37.5rem)`. A container is as wide as its context gives it, never as its content. container="env-window" makes the element a window of its own on purpose, such as a preview frame, whose content lays out at its window class; other `env-*` names are envUI's own.

props.name: padding
props.description: The inset on every side, a step of the spacing scale. None by default.

Breadcrumbs.description: The path from the top level to the current page; earlier levels are links.

props.name: items
props.description: From the top level to the current page, which is last.

props.name: wrap
props.description: The trail wraps onto more lines when it runs out of room; true by default. False keeps it on one line, for a bar or header: the current page is cut short first, and earlier levels keep their width.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark; name each trail where a page has several.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes for the `nav` element.

Button.description: Starts an action, or goes to a destination with href, in one of five variants and three tones, with optional icons. It renders a native button or link. An icon alone is an IconButton.

props.name: variant
props.description: The emphasis: primary for the main action of a view, secondary and outline for the rest, ghost for an application's chrome, such as a toolbar, and text for a link-like action. Without it, the button takes the variant its container gives where that variant takes its tone, such as ghost in a toolbar, and else primary.

props.name: tone
props.description: The meaning: neutral for most actions; accent, on a primary button only, for a rare consequential action, with 0.5 rem corners; danger for an action that deletes or ends something. Secondary buttons are always neutral.

props.name: underline
props.description: Show an underline for the text variant; defaults to false.

props.name: size
props.description: The height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale, such as sm for an action in a table cell or lg for the main call to action of a page. Without it, the button takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another. A button beside a field takes the field's size.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Fill the width of the container, such as the actions of a narrow form stacked in a column.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: A decorative icon before the label, such as an Add icon.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: A decorative icon after the label, such as a ChevronRight for a next step.

props.name: end
props.description: Quiet content at the far end, after the label, such as the Kbd of the shortcut that does the same: it takes the button's content color, keys in it are outlined caps with no fill, and in a button wider than its content, such as with fullWidth, it stays at the end while the icon and label stay at the start. Keys shown here take aria-hidden, and the button announces them with aria-keyshortcuts.

props.name: pending
props.description: Work started by this button is running: a spinner replaces the content without changing the button's size, and the button reports busy and ignores activation until pending ends.

props.name: disabled
props.description: A disabled button cannot be pressed; a disabled link has no destination, cannot be focused or followed, and reports aria-disabled.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination: the element is a native link, through the LinkProvider's link component.

ButtonGroup.description: Connected buttons keep their own outer corners and share the row inner radius.

props.name: orientation
props.description: A row of buttons, or a column in which every button is as wide as the group.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Fill the container's width, such as a sidebar's: in a row, labelled buttons share the room the icon-only ones leave, which keep their square size, and a row of icon-only buttons shares it evenly; in a column, every button is as wide as the group.

Calendar.description: A month of days to choose one from, following the WAI-ARIA date picker grid: the arrow keys move by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month (with Shift, by year), Home and End to the week's ends, and Enter or Space chooses the day. Named with aria-label or aria-labelledby, it is a group around the month's grid.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen day as YYYY-MM-DD, or null for none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The day an uncontrolled calendar starts with; none by default, which shows today's month.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the chosen day as YYYY-MM-DD.

props.name: min
props.description: The earliest day that can be chosen, as YYYY-MM-DD; earlier days are unavailable.

props.name: max
props.description: The latest day that can be chosen, as YYYY-MM-DD; later days are unavailable.

props.name: weekStart
props.description: The first day of each week, from 0 for Sunday to 6 for Saturday: by default the locale's, or Monday where the browser cannot tell.

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale of the month and weekday names and the day numbers: EnvUIProvider's, else the browser's. The days are always Gregorian, also in a locale with a calendar of its own.

props.name: previousMonthLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the previous month button.

props.name: nextMonthLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the next month button.

CalendarHeatmap.description: A calendar of daily values with weeks as columns and weekdays as rows, colored in steps of a tone. Each day names its date and value, shows them in a tooltip on hover and focus, and the grid is one tab stop that the arrow keys move through.

props.name: data
props.description: Values by day; days without an entry count as 0.

props.name: startDate
props.description: The first day shown, as YYYY-MM-DD; the earliest day in data by default.

props.name: endDate
props.description: The last day shown, as YYYY-MM-DD; the latest day in data by default.

props.name: levels
props.description: Color steps including the empty step, 2 to 10; 5 by default.

props.name: maxValue
props.description: The value that takes the strongest color; the largest value shown by default.

props.name: thresholds
props.description: The lowest value of each color step above the empty one, in ascending order, such as quantiles of the data to color by rank. Up to nine; they replace levels and maxValue. A day below the first threshold shows as empty, and a first threshold of 0 or less colors days of 0 too.

props.name: weekStart
props.description: The first day of each week column: 0 for Sunday (default) or 1 for Monday.

props.name: tone
props.description: The tone the colors are mixed from: accent by default.

props.name: formatValue
props.default: the number format of EnvUIProvider's locale, or else the browser's
props.description: Text for a value.

props.name: formatDate
props.default: the weekday, day, month and year in the locale, such as Tue 14 Oct 2025
props.description: Text for a day's date, in its accessible name and the default tooltip.

props.name: formatTooltip
props.description: Tooltip content for a day; the date and value by default.

props.name: monthLabels
props.default: the locale's short month names, from Intl
props.description: Twelve month names above the weeks, from January.

props.name: weekdayLabels
props.default: the locale's short weekday names, from Intl
props.description: Seven weekday names beside the rows, from Sunday.

props.name: lessLabel
props.description: Legend text before the lightest color. It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.calendarHeatmap.less`.

props.name: moreLabel
props.description: Legend text after the strongest color. It overrides EnvUIProvider's `messages.calendarHeatmap.more`.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the grid of days, such as "Deployments in the last year"; this or aria-labelledby.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of visible text that names the grid of days, such as a heading; this or aria-label.

Card.description: A rounded surface that groups content about one subject: a content card with an optional title row and actions, or one link or button.

props.name: background
props.description: The fill: muted, the standalone card fill; default, a quieter fill that groups content, such as a section of a settings page; or page, the page's own color, for a card inside a pane.

props.name: padding
props.default: 1.25 rem in narrow windows, growing to 1.5 rem from 50 rem wide
props.description: The inset on every side, as a step of the spacing scale, such as 6 for 2 rem; 0 removes it. Without it, the inset follows the window's width.

props.name: skeleton
props.description: Shows the component, and everything inside it, as a skeleton while its content loads: text becomes bars, icons, avatars, media and controls filled shapes of their size, and borders and corners stay. It is a busy region, and its content can't be focused or read until it loads. Turning it on or off renders its content anew, so state inside it starts over.

props.name: title
props.description: The card's title at the top: an `h3` in the title type. headingLevel sets another level. Given as undefined, such as over a placeholder item, a skeleton shows a bar in its place.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The title's heading level, for the page's outline; the type stays the title type.

props.name: meta
props.description: A short fact at the end of the title row, such as when the card was updated.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the title, in muted text.

props.name: actions
props.description: The card's controls, such as Buttons, in a strip along the bottom of the card.

props.name: render
props.description: The element for the card's meaning, such as render={<article />} or render={<section />}. A div by default.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination: the whole card is one native link, through the LinkProvider.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Runs when the card is pressed: the whole card is one native button.

props.name: disabled
props.description: A disabled link card has no destination, cannot be focused and reports aria-disabled; a disabled button card cannot be pressed.

Checkbox.description: A native checkbox inside its label, checked, unchecked or mixed.

props.name: ref
props.description: The native checkbox, so that a form library can register it and focus it; the other native props, such as name and required, reach it too.

props.name: className
props.description: The checkbox's class, on its root element, the label around the box and the text.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the root element.

props.name: label
props.description: The text beside the box, which names the checkbox; pressing it toggles the checkbox.

props.name: checked
props.description: Whether the box is checked, unchecked or "mixed", for a parent whose children are partly chosen. With `onCheckedChange` it controls the checkbox.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: How an uncontrolled checkbox starts, and what a form reset restores; unchecked by default.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Called with the new state when people press the checkbox; a mixed checkbox reports true.

Code.description: Inline source in the code theme of the app theme; use CodeBlock for multiline source.

CodeBlock.description: Source display in the code theme of the app theme, with that code theme's own colors; copy always uses the original string. Its words come from EnvUIProvider's messages.codeBlock.

props.name: children
props.description: The source, as one string; it is shown, highlighted and copied as it is.

props.name: language
props.description: The language to highlight: js, jsx, ts, tsx, java, json, html, xml, css, sql, sh, bash, yaml, md or ini, or their full names. Other values, and none, leave the source plain text.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the block in its heading and for assistive technology, such as a file name.

props.name: copyable
props.description: Shows a copy button in the heading that copies the source; false by default.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Wraps long lines instead of scrolling them; false by default.

CodeDiff.description: The changes between two versions of a file, rendered by Diffs (diffs.com) in the code theme of the app theme, as code blocks are; the whole file when nothing changed.

props.name: before
props.description: The source before the change.

props.name: after
props.description: The source after the change.

props.name: filename
props.description: Names the file in the header and chooses its language, such as form.json.

props.name: language
props.description: Overrides the language the file name implies, such as json.

props.name: header
props.description: Shows the file header with its name and change counts; true by default.

props.name: expandUnchanged
props.description: Shows the unchanged lines between changes instead of folding them; false by default.

props.name: layout
props.description: auto (default) sets old and new side by side from 56 rem of width; unified keeps one column.

ColorPicker.description: A compact color picker on React Aria's color hooks: a square saturation and brightness area with a vertical hue slider, and an alpha slider with `alpha`, at its side; under them, a format select, the browser's eyedropper where it has one, a copy button, and fields for the chosen format, or the fields of several `formats` together, each with its own copy button; and preset swatches. Every part works with the keyboard; the channels and the area are named in the EnvUIProvider's language.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label above the picker. Set false where something else names it, such as the popover around it: the label still names the picker for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the picker, such as where the color shows.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the picker that says what is wrong with the color, such as too little contrast.

props.name: label
props.description: The color's name, such as Accent color; it names the picker, and ColorPickerButton's popover and button.

props.name: value
props.description: The color in a controlled picker: a CSS color string, such as #6750a4, rgb(103, 80, 164) or hsl(256, 34%, 48%), or React Aria's Color; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The color an uncontrolled picker starts at, and that a form reset restores.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the color as it changes, as a string in valueFormat, such as #6750a4, and as React Aria's Color, which keeps the hue of a gray and converts to any format.

props.name: valueFormat
props.description: The format of the string onValueChange receives and a form submits: hex (#rrggbb, or #rrggbbaa while translucent), rgb (rgb() or rgba()) or hsl (hsl() or hsla()).

props.name: formats
props.description: The formats whose fields show together, one under another in this order, such as `['hex', 'rgb', 'hsl']`. With one, the picker shows that format alone; without the prop, it shows one format at a time, hex first, with a select that switches to RGB or HSL.

props.name: alpha
props.description: Whether the color has an alpha: a slider and a field for its opacity, and a value with its alpha while translucent. Without it, colors are opaque.

props.name: eyeDropper
props.description: Whether to show the eyedropper, which picks a color from the screen, where the browser has one (Chromium-based browsers on the desktop); elsewhere it never shows.

props.name: copy
props.description: Whether to show the button that copies the color, as the fields show it.

props.name: swatches
props.description: Preset colors to choose from, under the fields: CSS color strings, React Aria's Colors, or `{ color, label }` with a name, such as the colors of a brand.

props.name: name
props.description: Submits the color with a form under this name, as a string in valueFormat.

props.name: form
props.description: The id of the form the color submits with, where the picker sits outside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the picker takes no input, faded.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether people can read and copy the color, but not change it.

ColorPickerButton.description: A compact button that shows a color as a swatch and its value, and opens a ColorPicker in a Popover: the common way to choose a color in a toolbar, a row or a form. The button is named after the label and the color, such as Accent color, #6750A4.

props.name: className
props.description: The button's class, beside env-color-picker-button.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the button.

props.name: size
props.description: The button's height, as on every control; without it, its container's.

props.name: side
props.description: The side of the button the picker opens on.

props.name: align
props.description: How the picker lines up with the button along that side.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the picker starts open, such as in a picture of it.

props.name: label
props.description: The color's name, such as Accent color; it names the picker, and ColorPickerButton's popover and button.

props.name: value
props.description: The color in a controlled picker: a CSS color string, such as #6750a4, rgb(103, 80, 164) or hsl(256, 34%, 48%), or React Aria's Color; update it from onValueChange.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The color an uncontrolled picker starts at, and that a form reset restores.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the color as it changes, as a string in valueFormat, such as #6750a4, and as React Aria's Color, which keeps the hue of a gray and converts to any format.

props.name: valueFormat
props.description: The format of the string onValueChange receives and a form submits: hex (#rrggbb, or #rrggbbaa while translucent), rgb (rgb() or rgba()) or hsl (hsl() or hsla()).

props.name: formats
props.description: The formats whose fields show together, one under another in this order, such as `['hex', 'rgb', 'hsl']`. With one, the picker shows that format alone; without the prop, it shows one format at a time, hex first, with a select that switches to RGB or HSL.

props.name: alpha
props.description: Whether the color has an alpha: a slider and a field for its opacity, and a value with its alpha while translucent. Without it, colors are opaque.

props.name: eyeDropper
props.description: Whether to show the eyedropper, which picks a color from the screen, where the browser has one (Chromium-based browsers on the desktop); elsewhere it never shows.

props.name: copy
props.description: Whether to show the button that copies the color, as the fields show it.

props.name: swatches
props.description: Preset colors to choose from, under the fields: CSS color strings, React Aria's Colors, or `{ color, label }` with a name, such as the colors of a brand.

props.name: name
props.description: Submits the color with a form under this name, as a string in valueFormat.

props.name: form
props.description: The id of the form the color submits with, where the picker sits outside it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the picker takes no input, faded.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether people can read and copy the color, but not change it.

ColorSwatch.description: A small rounded sample of a color, with a hairline edge that keeps light and dark colors visible on every surface and a checkerboard under a translucent one. With `format`, it writes the color's value beside it, and with `label`, a name. Alone, it is an image named by the color's description, such as dark purple, in the EnvUIProvider's language; as a Button's icon it is decorative, and the button's text names the color.

props.name: color
props.description: The color it shows: a CSS color string, such as #6750a4, rgb(103, 80, 164) or hsl(256, 34%, 48%), with an optional alpha, or React Aria's Color.

props.name: format
props.description: Writes the color beside the sample in this format: hex, such as #6750A4, rgb or hsl. Without it and a label, the sample stands alone, named by the color's description, such as dark purple.

props.name: label
props.description: A name beside the sample, before the value, such as the label the color belongs to.

props.name: size
props.description: The sample's size: sm, 0.75 rem, for dense rows; md, 1 rem, the size of an icon. As a Button's icon it takes the icon's size.

Column.description: Lays its direct children out one under another, `gap` apart, such as a form's fields. A flex column that sizes to its content and never paints.

props.name: gap
props.description: The space between the direct children, a step of the spacing scale. None by default.

props.name: align
props.description: How the children line up across the line: stretch, the default, makes each as wide as a column or as tall as a row, except controls such as buttons, which keep their own size; start, center and end keep every child at its own size.

props.name: justify
props.description: Where the children sit along the line when there is room to spare: at the start, in the center, at the end, such as a form's actions, or between, spread out to the edges.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, for its meaning, such as render={<section />} or render={<ul />}, or another component to lay out without a wrapper, such as a Surface: the primitive's attributes merge into its props. It must forward native props and refs. A div by default.

props.name: ref
props.description: The rendered element, a div by default. Its type is the element type parameter, which a ref passed in sets: a ref to the element that render makes, such as useRef<HTMLElement>(null) with render={<section />}, type-checks.

props.name: name
props.description: A name for this node, such as "filters" or "summary", which dev mode and the docs show; it renders as `data-env-name`. A component's part class names its node instead.

props.name: container
props.description: Makes the element a size container of this name, for container queries on its inline size, such as container="filters" for `@container filters (width >= 37.5rem)`. A container is as wide as its context gives it, never as its content. container="env-window" makes the element a window of its own on purpose, such as a preview frame, whose content lays out at its window class; other `env-*` names are envUI's own.

props.name: padding
props.description: The inset on every side, a step of the spacing scale. None by default.

Combobox.description: A text field that filters a list of options as people type, for choosing one option or several. Chosen options show as removable chips; keyboard, focus and announcements follow the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern.

props.name: ref
props.description: The text input, so that a form library can register it and focus it.

props.name: className
props.description: The field's class, on its root element, beside env-field and env-combobox.

props.name: style
props.description: Styles of the field's root element.

props.name: items
props.description: The options, or groups of options under headings, in display order.

props.name: filter
props.description: Which options match the typed text: by default those whose label or description contains it, ignoring case and accents. null shows the items as given, for searching on the server.

props.name: onInputValueChange
props.description: Receives the typed text, and an empty string once it is cleared, such as to search a server.

props.name: loading
props.description: The options are loading: the popup shows loadingLabel instead of emptyLabel.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.description: Shown in the popup while loading.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Shown in the popup when no option matches.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look, as TextField's: outline, at the control height, or floating, 3.5 rem tall with room for its label, for long forms on a page.

props.name: size
props.description: The field's height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale. Without it, the field takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another. The popup's rows take the row height of the scale.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label inside the field, where it floats into the outline while the field has focus or a value. Set false for a field whose purpose is clear without it; a placeholder then gives the visible guidance.

props.name: clearable
props.description: A clear button removes the value while there is one; Esc on the closed field clears it too.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the clear button.

props.name: removeLabel
props.default: Remove followed by the label, or EnvUIProvider's messages.combobox.remove
props.description: Accessible name of a chip's remove button, from the chip's label.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the list is open; with `onOpenChange` it controls the popup.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled list starts open; closed by default.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called as the popup opens and closes, such as to load the options as it opens.

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale of the default filter's matching: EnvUIProvider's, else the browser's.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: description
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the description.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Several options can be chosen; they show as chips in the field.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen option's value, or null for none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value an uncontrolled field starts with, and that a form reset restores; none by default.

props.name: onValueChange
props.type: ((value: string | null, item: Item | null) => void) | ((value: string[], items: Item[]) => void)
props.description: Receives the chosen value and its option, or null twice once the field is cleared.

CommandPalette.description: A quick-open dialog near the top of the window: a search field over a list of options the application filters and ranks, built on Base UI's Autocomplete inside a dialog. The arrow keys move the highlight while typing continues, and the number of results is announced as it changes. className, style, ref and data attributes go to the dialog's surface.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the palette is open; the application opens it, such as from a shortcut.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with false when Esc, a press on the backdrop or a choice closes the palette.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the dialog, the search field and the list.

props.name: inputValue
props.description: The text in the search field.

props.name: onInputValueChange
props.description: Receives the text as people type.

props.name: items
props.description: Filtered and ranked by the application, in display order.

props.name: onAction
props.description: Enter or a press on an option; Ctrl or Cmd sets modifier.

props.name: closeOnAction
props.description: Close after an option is chosen.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown in the empty search field, such as "Search documents by name or folder".

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Shown in place of the list when there are no items, and announced.

props.name: hints
props.description: Key hints below the list, such as { keys: ['Enter'], label: 'Open' }.

props.name: footer
props.description: Other content below the list, after the hints.

Composer.description: The message field of a conversation: a multiline field on a raised surface that grows with its text up to maxRows, with a send button at the end that becomes a stop button while running. Enter submits, Shift+Enter starts a new line and an input method's composition never submits. Without onSubmit, Enter and the send button submit the field's form.

props.name: value
props.description: The message text of a controlled composer.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The starting text of an uncontrolled composer; it clears after each submit through onSubmit and when its form resets.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Receives the text as it changes, and an empty string when an uncontrolled composer clears.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Enter or the send button submits the text as typed, and an uncontrolled composer clears. Blank text never submits, and neither does a disabled, running or pending composer. Without onSubmit, they submit the field's form instead and the text stays until the form resets. Without onSubmit or a form there is nothing to send: the button is unavailable and Enter starts a new line.

props.name: pending
props.description: A send is in progress, such as a request the application makes: sending is unavailable while the field stays editable and keeps focus. The pending action of an enclosing form counts too; set pending for a form the field joins through its form attribute, or for a request of the application's own.

props.name: running
props.description: A reply is on its way: the send button becomes a stop button and Enter does not submit.

props.name: onStop
props.description: Called by the stop button while running; it stays available when the field is disabled.

props.name: sendLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the send button.

props.name: stopLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the stop button.

props.name: minRows
props.description: Lines the field shows while empty; 1 by default.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: Lines the field grows to before it scrolls; 8 by default.

props.name: start
props.description: Content at the start of the action row, such as an attach button or the name of a model.

props.name: footer
props.description: Supporting text below the composer, such as a note on attachments; it describes the field.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the field, which has no visible label, such as "Message"; this or aria-labelledby.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of visible text that names the field; this or aria-label.

ConfirmButton.description: A button for an action that takes effect at once and cannot be undone. The first press arms it and names the consequence in place; a second press runs it. It disarms after a few seconds, when focus leaves and on Escape.

props.name: end
props.description: Quiet content at the far end, after the label, such as the Kbd of the shortcut that does the same: it takes the button's content color, keys in it are outlined caps with no fill, and in a button wider than its content, such as with fullWidth, it stays at the end while the icon and label stay at the start. Keys shown here take aria-hidden, and the button announces them with aria-keyshortcuts.

props.name: size
props.description: The height, as on every control: sm, md or lg in the current scale, such as sm for an action in a table cell or lg for the main call to action of a page. Without it, the button takes the control height of its container, md unless the container sets another. A button beside a field takes the field's size.

props.name: underline
props.description: Show an underline for the text variant; defaults to false.
